extracted.intended_audience: Authors, Reviewers, Area Chairs (ACs), Senior Area Chairs (SACs), and Program Chairs for NeurIPS 2026 Main Track
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation standards for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and adjudicating NeurIPS 2026 Main Track papers, including ethical, reproducibility, formatting, and meta-review rules for reviewers/ACs/SACs. Covers submission mechanics, review rubrics, conflict policies, and program-committee responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview profile requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors, reviewers, ACs, and SACs must have an active OpenReview profile by the abstract submission deadline; profiles must be up to date with publications and affiliations and are used to inform conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importing publications via DBLP is the easiest option but not required; missing or incorrect profiles risk desk rejection (for authors) and sanctions (for reviewers). New profiles without institutional email are moderated and may take up to two weeks to activate. Keep preferred contact email current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional eligibility for submissions follows the U.S. State Department Guidelines (as referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the referenced guidelines to confirm eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: All participants must declare domain conflicts and personal conflicts in OpenReview. Domain conflicts are entered in Education & Career History and hide submissions when overlapping; personal conflicts are entered in Advisors & Other Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the last three years of Education & Career History are used for domain conflicts. Personal conflicts include family/close personal relationships, PhD advisor/advisee, and all co-authors on original research articles in the last three years (perspective pieces do not count). You may mark other significant conflicts as hidden and visible only to Program Chairs; false declarations to manipulate assignment may lead to rejection without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-collusion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS prohibits deceptive bidding or collusion where authors cooperate with reviewers, ACs, or SACs to obtain favorable reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If collusion is identified, involved parties will be notified and can respond; program chairs' decision is final. Penalties include removal from reviewing, rejection of all papers under consideration, sharing identities with sister conferences, informing institutions, and future sanctions. Collusion may be identified at any point in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers, ACs, SACs, and PCs must keep everything related to the review process confidential and must not share or discuss submission content with unauthorized parties or unsanctioned LLMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they are public and permission is granted. Submitted code may not be distributed or used outside the review process. If external reviewer support is needed, formally invite them through OpenReview. Do not ask others (not assigned) about their assigned reviews; this is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS Code of Ethics adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions and participants must adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, which complements the Code of Conduct and addresses research ethics and societal/environmental impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Code of Ethics informs the Submission Checklist and details expectations about ethical practices; violations may lead to rejection and other penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS expects adherence to academic integrity policies (see NeurIPS Academic Integrity policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and reviewers should consult the referenced policy for definitions and procedures related to integrity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair wages and human-subjects requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving human subjects or participants must ensure fair wages and follow institutional protocols (e.g., IRB) or equivalent informal review when no formal process exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crowdsourcing or contract workers must be paid at least the regional minimum hourly rate. When no formal IRB exists, consider peer or internal ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasets should minimize exposure of personally identifiable information unless explicit informed consent is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using real people's data, authors must obtain explicit consent or explain why consent was not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent for datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Any paper that creates a dataset with real people should obtain explicit consent from participants or explain why consent could not be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document consent procedures in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecated datasets policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must confirm that datasets they use are still available and not taken down by the original creators; datasets removed by creators should not be used except for audit or critical assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the NeurIPS list of deprecated datasets for known cases and include justification if using deprecated data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and license compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must respect defined dataset licenses (e.g., CC 4.0, MIT) and evolving norms of fair use in ML research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe license terms and adhere to restrictions; consult resources linked in the handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative evaluation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: When collecting or choosing datasets, authors should assess and report how representative the datasets are of the intended population and substantiate claims of diversity or universality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of representation must be supported by concrete evidence or examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact considerations (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should transparently communicate known or anticipated consequences of research and consider specific concern areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be done via the paper checklist or a dedicated section; not required to be titled 'broader impacts' but must fit within page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether technology could be used to harm, injure, or kill people (direct application, side effects, or misuse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NeurIPS does not accept research whose primary goal is to increase lethality of weapons systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Security
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether applications open security vulnerabilities or could cause serious accidents when deployed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If risks exist, recommend or implement protections against security risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the technology could discriminate, exclude, or negatively impact people (e.g., in healthcare, education, credit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should evaluate potential discriminatory impacts and mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Surveillance
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using bulk surveillance data without consulting local laws; do not use surveillance to predict protected attributes or endanger people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult relevant legislation before collecting/analyzing surveillance data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Deception & Harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider risks related to deceptive interactions such as fraud, impersonation, political influence, or enabling hate speech/abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe whether the approach could facilitate such harms and mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider environmental impacts, e.g., promoting fossil fuel extraction or producing high greenhouse gas emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify emissions where appropriate and consider climate impact mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Human rights
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS prohibits research that builds upon or facilitates illegal activity and discourages work that could deny people fundamental rights (privacy, speech, health, liberty, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions do not directly facilitate human-rights violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact — Bias and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify suspected biases or limitations in models or datasets and inspect whether they encode or exacerbate bias against protected groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report analyses, limitations, and any mitigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact mitigation — documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers should provide data and model documentation (e.g., model cards, datasheets) as part of submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured templates linked in the handbook to communicate dataset/model details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact mitigation — licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: If releasing data or models, provide licenses that state intended use and limitations to prevent misuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document license and restrictions in the paper and repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact mitigation — secure storage & distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use privacy protocols, encryption, and anonymization for storing/distributing sensitive data; employ stronger measures for biometric/medical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe measures used and rationale in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact mitigation — responsible release
rubrics_metrics.description: High-risk or dual-use models should be released with safeguards (e.g., controlled access, codes of conduct); vulnerability disclosures should follow responsible disclosure procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain release strategy and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact mitigation — allow access to artifacts for scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: When releasing artifacts, provide information needed to understand them (code, environment versions, weights, hyperparameters) to enable auditing and external scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For accepted papers, de-anonymized links should be provided to support reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact mitigation — disclose elements for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should include sufficient information for reproduction: code, data, model weights, hyperparameters, and compute resources needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include descriptions and/or actual artifacts; use the paper checklist to ensure required elements are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact mitigation — legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure awareness of regional legal requirements and consult specialists where appropriate; provide additional information if legal compliance could not be met due to human-rights concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include consulting law clinics for IP and technology law issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations reporting and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Violations of the Code of Ethics should be reported to hotline@neurips.cc; NeurIPS may reject works or impose penalties (removal from reviewing, revoking publication, sharing identities, institutional reporting, future sanctions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NeurIPS can investigate at any time, including post-acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper formatting and file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be a single PDF in the provided LaTeX template; main text limited to nine content pages (figures/tables included); references, appendices, and checklist do not count as content pages; maximum file size 50MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the provided LaTeX template is accepted; Microsoft Word template discontinued. Submissions that alter margins/fonts to bypass limits may be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization and double-blind policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must be anonymized and contain no identifying information in the paper or supplementary materials (including code); self-citations must be written to preserve anonymity (e.g., 'In the previous work of Smith et al. [1]...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If citing an anonymized submission, include an anonymized copy in the supplement. Violations of anonymization may lead to desk rejection. Authors are responsible for ensuring linked materials are anonymously browsable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author list and submission timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All author names must be entered by the abstract submission deadline; after this deadline, changes are limited to author order only; if accepted, no additions/removals of authors are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may withdraw submissions at any time during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution type selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must choose a contribution type (General, Theory, Use-Inspired, Concept & Feasibility, Negative Results); reviewers interpret criteria in light of the chosen type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs and reviewers will be provided guidelines on interpreting standard reviewing criteria for different contribution types; choose the type that best fits the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary code and data submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit supplementary material (code/data) in a single ZIP up to 100MB; supplementary material must be anonymized and created by the authors to directly support submission content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged to upload code to help reviewers assess quality. Reviewers must keep code/data confidential and use only for review. For accepted papers, provide de-anonymized links for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Code should include training and evaluation scripts, dependency specification, and ideally be self-contained and executable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If code is not executable, explain why (e.g., specialized hardware, proprietary libraries). Follow linked best-practices resources (e.g., PapersWithCode guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data submission and dataset best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: For new datasets, answer checklist questions, link to dataset (anonymized for review), place datasets in repositories ensuring long-term preservation, assign persistent identifiers, adhere to metadata standards, and describe licenses/access restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If impossible to meet suggestions, include justification in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper checklist completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to complete the included paper checklist to reflect on reproducibility, transparency, ethics, and societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist is part of the template; completing it helps authors reflect on responsible research practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author use of agents and LLMs policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of agents/LLMs as important, original, or non-standard components must be documented in experimental setup; basic editing/grammar checks and basic code assistance do not need documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for ensuring all content is correct and original; LLMs cannot be listed as authors. Attempts to manipulate reviewing (prompt injections etc.) are prohibited. Document non-standard LLM uses (e.g., LLM as search heuristic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-anonymous preprints (arXiv, personal sites) are allowed and will not result in rejection; if using NeurIPS style for preprints use the 'preprint' option not the 'final' option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public versions should not say 'Under review at NeurIPS'. Reviewers are instructed not to actively seek preprints, but encountering one is not a conflict. Aggressive advertising of papers under submission may be considered violating the double-blind policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting the same archival work to multiple venues with overlapping authors is treated as prior work and is prohibited; thin-slicing similar papers to multiple venues is prohibited; submitting to NeurIPS and then to another archival venue while NeurIPS review is ongoing is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations are grounds for desk rejection at any point in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporaneous work handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers appearing online after March 1, 2026 are generally considered contemporaneous and will not be cause for rejection based solely on comparison; authors should cite and discuss contemporaneous work as feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions very similar to contemporaneous work will undergo extra scrutiny for plagiarism/missing credit. Date-of-publication judgements will be handled by the area chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and ACs can flag submissions for ethics review; flagged submissions are sent to an ethics review committee whose comments are visible to authors and considered by reviewers and ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics reviewers cannot directly reject, but Program Chairs may reject on ethical grounds regardless of scientific quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS does not tolerate plagiarism; identified plagiarism will trigger notification, response opportunity, and potential penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification can occur anytime during review; penalties include removal from reviewing system, rejection of papers, sharing identities, and institutional sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible reviewing policy for reviewer-authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who are reviewers will not see reviews of their own submissions unless they have completed all assigned reviews; late reviews cause loss of access to reviews of own papers; gross negligence may lead to desk rejection sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviews are late, co-authors lose access until completion of their professional reviews (maximally until two days before end of rebuttal period). PCs may desk-reject papers at meta-review stage for gross negligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible ACing policy for AC-authors
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs who are authors will not see reviews/meta-reviews of their own papers unless they have completed all assigned meta-reviews; late meta-reviews cause loss of access; gross negligence may lead to desk rejection sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs should engage with reviewers; failure to produce thoughtful meta-reviews may trigger sanctions including desk rejection of the AC's own papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response (rebuttal) rules and phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Author response period has three phases (initial response, author-reviewer discussion, reviewer-AC discussion). Authors may not submit revised papers or supplemental files; rebuttal per-review character limit is 10,000 characters; allowed plain text with Markdown; cannot upload additional files; no links except anonymized code link requested by reviewers to AC via Official Comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should clarify reviewer/AC questions and not serve as rushed revisions. Responses may include new results but original submission remains the basis for acceptance decisions. Rebuttals must be anonymized and avoid identifying information.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenReview mechanics for rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should respond to each review using Rebuttal buttons, set correct readers, and respect per-review limits and formatting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the AC can receive anonymized code links via Official Comment if reviewers request code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-accept camera-ready requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera-ready submission: combine up to 10 pages of main paper, references, text appendices, and checklist into a single PDF; de-anonymized links for code/data are encouraged; editors may allow minor changes to title, keywords, abstract but not substantive differences; reordering authors allowed but no additions/removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must upload a paragraph-length lay summary for public consumption. Minor edits allowed for a short period after conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding transparency statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Camera-ready paper must include funding and competing interests disclosures covering the last 36 months; list funding that supported the submitted work and other financial relationships that could be perceived to influence the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples (grants, donated GPUs, employment, honoraria, travel support, hardware donations). If primary affiliation is listed, it need not be repeated in competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author registration and presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: At least one author of each accepted paper must register for and attend the main conference in person (virtual-only passes not sufficient); each accepted poster must be presented at the main conference or an official satellite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors cannot attend, they must arrange someone to present. Failure to register/present may lead to revocation of accepted publication status or downgrading of orals to posters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility guidelines for talks and posters
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentations should use minimal text, large fonts, high-contrast color palettes, avoid flashing graphics, avoid relying on color alone, and use examples understandable to diverse audiences; avoid offensive imagery/text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow W3C, ACM, and RECSYS guides; when speaking, do not assume all can see slides—describe important content verbally. Choose color palettes accessible to color-blind viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid selection for student authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper may designate one student author email for financial aid consideration; the student must confirm need and agree to volunteer if selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students must fill out the Financial Aid application when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer task flow and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should prepare by reading the Code of Conduct and handbook, bid on papers, check assignments for conflicts, and complete timely, high-quality reviews according to deadlines and policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids are important for matching; report conflicts promptly. Reviewers may be reminded multiple times; if unable to complete, seek replacement or inform ACs. Keep reviews respectful and constructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review content structure — strengths & weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should discuss strengths and weaknesses clearly and provide actionable feedback; reviewers are asked to list ~3–5 key questions or suggestions that could change the score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear criteria under which the evaluation could increase or decrease to help productive rebuttal and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing criterion — Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality assesses correctness, soundness, rigor of methods and evaluation and whether results are convincing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must justify numerical rating in 'Strengths and Weaknesses' text. Use accompanying numerical scale (4-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing criterion — Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity evaluates how well the paper is written, organized, and whether the arguments and evidence are communicated effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity rating should reflect the discussion of strengths/weaknesses. Use numerical scale (4-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing criterion — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance considers the impact of the contribution: whether it affects one or more areas of AI and the degree of advance it represents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider evaluation, reproducibility, resources, and ethical considerations when rating. Use numerical scale (4-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing criterion — Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality asks whether the work provides new insights, deepens understanding, introduces novel tasks/metrics/methods, or offers novel combinations with well-articulated reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality does not require an entirely new method; novel analysis or improved efficiency/fairness is valuable. Use numerical scale (4-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical rating scales for subcriteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assign numerical ratings for Quality, Clarity, Significance, and Originality on a 4-to-1 scale: 4=excellent, 3=good, 2=fair, 1=poor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratings should be supported by the written strengths/weaknesses section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall recommendation scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an overall score on a 6-to-1 scale with defined labels: 6 (Strong Accept), 5 (Accept), 4 (Borderline accept), 3 (Borderline reject), 2 (Reject), 1 (Strong Reject). Examples of when to use each label are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use '4' and '3' sparingly for borderline cases. Consider technical quality, evaluation, reproducibility, and ethical considerations in choosing the overall score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidence score
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a confidence score (5 to 1) indicating how certain the reviewer is about their assessment and familiarity with the work and related literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 = absolutely certain (checked math/details), down to 1 = an educated guess (out of area or difficult to understand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions and actionable suggestions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must list up to ~3–5 careful, actionable questions and suggestions focusing on key points that, if addressed, could change the reviewer's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete guidance and be explicit about what would change the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and societal impact evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should assess whether authors have adequately addressed limitations and potential negative societal impacts; if adequately addressed, simply leave 'yes', otherwise provide constructive suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be rewarded for honest limitations disclosure; reviewers should note missing critical points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flagging
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are ethical issues with a paper, reviewers should flag the paper for ethics review as per Code of Ethics guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on when to flag is in the Code of Ethics; flagged papers get comments from ethics reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct & responsible reviewing acknowledgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must acknowledge that they will abide by the NeurIPS Code of Conduct and the responsible reviewing initiatives including LLM use guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must tick acknowledgement statements in the review form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review timing and content guidance for ACs
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial meta-review is due before the author response period; it should outline what authors need to address to change acceptance outcome and categorize papers into 'toward rejection', 'need clarification', or 'plan to accept'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on key, prioritized issues that, if successfully rebutted, would change the AC's view; avoid unreasonable requests. Counter perceived reviewer biases and be familiar with all assigned papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: AC discussion and moderation duties
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs must initiate and lead discussions when author responses are posted, ensure reviewers engage, moderate respectfully, and steer discussions toward critical aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure reviewers respond to all author responses and keep reviewers focused on key issues. ACs can use restricted-visibility comments as needed (authors, reviewers, SACs, PCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final meta-review expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Final meta-review should indicate whether author responses addressed issues and explain the decision (accept/reject/borderline); if overruling unanimous referees, provide justifications as thorough as a full review and consider soliciting auxiliary reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be decisive on borderline papers and discuss decisions with SAC for calibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAC oversight and calibration duties
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs oversee ACs, ensure reviewing quality, help secure emergency reviewers, calibrate decisions across ACs, and discuss all proposed decisions with Program Chairs during final decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SACs should proactively check-in with ACs, be responsive, and demonstrate empathy for personal circumstances affecting timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency reviewing and ensuring review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs and SACs must ensure papers have sufficient quality reviews; if a reviewer cannot deliver, find replacement reviewers and, if reviews are substandard, ask reviewers to improve with polite, concrete guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag questionable papers for ethics review and assign ethics reviewers who join the paper's program committee as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and opt-in for rejected papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews, meta-reviews, and discussions will be public for accepted papers (anonymized identities). Rejected authors have two weeks after notification to opt in to make their de-anonymized rejected papers public on OpenReview (they remain marked as rejected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer/AC/SAC identities remain anonymous for published reviews of accepted papers.
